data.one_liner: iOS CallKit and Android ConnectionService bindings for Flutter
data.what_it_does: Provides native iOS CallKit and Android ConnectionService bindings to show native incoming call screens and handle audio calls in Flutter apps. Supports displaying incoming calls, making outgoing calls, and handling call events.
use_when: You are building a VoIP, audio, or video calling app in Flutter
You need native incoming call integration on iOS using CallKit
You need native connection management on Android
avoid_when: Your app does not involve real-time phone calls or VoIP
You only need local push notifications without native call UI behavior
strengths: Integrates with platform-native calling interfaces like iOS CallKit
Supports Android custom UI and ConnectionService bindings
Allows event handling for call acceptance, declining, and starting
weaknesses: Requires significant native setup for both Android (permissions, activity launch mode) and iOS (PushKit, AppDelegate configuration)
Push handling on iOS must be written in native Swift code due to restrictions
data.setup_notes: Requires modifying AndroidManifest.xml (singleInstance launchMode, notification permissions), Info.plist (background modes), and AppDelegate.swift for iOS PushKit VoIP handling.
